candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 42 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 43 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 44 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 45 not required. 46
candidates.context: While the guidance discusses situations in which it is appropriate to consider overall survival for 34 the primary endpoint, this guidance primarily focuses on statistical or design considerations 35 when overall survival is not the primary endpoint. Additionally, this guidance focuses on the 36 assessment of overall survival in randomized trials. In general, time-to-event endpoints (e.g., 37 overall survival, progression-free survival, etc.) are challenging to interpret in single-arm trials 38 due to the lack of a randomized control arm to demonstrate that the experimental treatment 39 results in an improvement in the time-to-event endpoint. 40

candidates.statement: Overall survival should be prioritized as the primary endpoint when feasible. It is most 57 appropriate for consideration in randomized trials of oncologic diseases with a short natural 58 history (e.g., metastatic pancreatic cancer), late-line disease settings, or in disease settings where 59 there are other therapeutics known to prolong overall survival and it is important to demonstrate 60 retention or improvement of this survival advantage. 61
candidates.context: Overall survival is both an efficacy and a safety endpoint; it can be favorably impacted by the 51 therapeutic benefits of a specific drug and negatively impacted by the drug’s toxicity. Overall 52 survival is also an objective, clinically meaningful endpoint that can be measured easily and 53 precisely. It is considered a gold standard endpoint in oncology, as prolongation of life in the 54 setting of a life-threatening disease is of clear inherent value. 55 In certain oncology settings, it is often not feasible or practical to include overall survival as the 63 primary endpoint. In some indolent diseases or those with extremely efficacious therapeutics that 64 result in long survival times, the follow-up time needed to show superiority of overall survival as 65 the primary endpoint may be impractical. Additionally, as mentioned, overall survival may not be 66 appropriate in single-arm

candidates.statement: This section includes considerations for pre-specification of statistical analyses, assessments for 210 harm, and post hoc analyses of overall survival. Sponsors should, a priori, specify the statistical 211 analyses of overall survival, prior to knowledge of any study results or data unblinding, in a 212 clinical trial protocol or accompanying separate document (e.g., SAP). If the protocol and SAP 213 do not adequately characterize plans for assessing, measuring, or analyzing overall survival, 214 evaluations of overall survival may be considered post hoc. FDA also considers additional 215 analyses conducted on overall survival outside the scope of those pre-specified in the SAP to be 216 post hoc and for exploratory purposes (e.g., for hypothesis generation). 217

However, such 496 findings may be sufficient to raise safety concerns, warranting further investigation. 497

candidates.statement: • If there is a known subgroup with potentially poor survival, this subgroup may be 509 excluded from enrollment if there is sufficient prior knowledge that these patients would 510 not benefit from the therapy. Alternatively, if these patients are included in the trial, early 511 interim subgroup analyses should be pre-specified to mitigate concern for potential harm, 512 particularly in cases where patients require longer term therapy and where there is 513 expected to be a sufficient number of events in the subgroup. 514
candidates.context: — Subgroup analyses indicating potential detrimental overall survival could result in 506 halting the trial, indication restrictions, or post-marketing requirements. 507 • In addition to pre-specified subgroup analyses, additional post hoc analyses to explore 516 relevant subgroups can be used to investigate any safety concerns in a successful trial. 517
